items.headline: RBI constitutes committee to frame responsible AI framework for financial sector
items.text: The Reserve Bank of India constituted a committee chaired by Dr. Pushpak Bhattacharyya to recommend a framework for the responsible and ethical use of artificial intelligence.

items.headline: Winter Session concludes: four Bills introduced, one passed by both Houses
items.text: The Winter Session of Parliament, held from November 25 to December 20, 2024, concluded with four Bills introduced. Only one Bill, the Bharatiya Vayuyan Vidheyak, 2024, was passed by both Houses.

items.headline: Conduct of Election Rules amended to limit public inspection of certain election papers
items.text: The Ministry of Law and Justice issued the Conduct of Elections (Second Amendment) Rules, 2024, amending the Conduct of Election Rules, 1961 framed under the Representation of the People Act, 1951. The amendment changes which election papers are open to public inspection.

items.headline: Parliament passes Bharatiya Vayuyan Vidheyak, 2024 to replace the Aircraft Act, 1934
items.text: The Bharatiya Vayuyan Vidheyak, 2024, which seeks to replace the Aircraft Act, 1934, was passed by both Houses of Parliament during the Winter Session that concluded on December 20, 2024. It was the only Bill passed in the session.

items.headline: Coastal Shipping Bill and Merchant Shipping Bill, 2024 introduced in Lok Sabha
items.text: During the Winter Session that ended on December 20, 2024, the Coastal Shipping Bill, 2024 was introduced in Lok Sabha to regulate vessels trading in Indian coastal waters, and the Merchant Shipping Bill, 2024 was introduced to replace the Merchant Shipping Act, 1958.

items.body: Securities and Exchange Board of India
items.headline: SEBI board approves changes to SME listing framework and other decisions
items.text: At its board meeting, SEBI approved decisions relating to the framework for SME listings, governance of AI tools used by regulated entities, and thresholds applicable to debt-listed entities.

items.headline: Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill for simultaneous elections introduced, sent to JPC
items.text: The Constitution (One Hundred and Twenty-Ninth Amendment) Bill, 2024, which provides for simultaneous elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies, was introduced in Lok Sabha. It was referred to a 39-member Joint Parliamentary Committee chaired by P.P. Chaudhary.
items.why: First formal legislative step towards 'One Nation, One Election'.

items.headline: Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024 introduced to align UT assembly polls
items.text: The Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024 was introduced in Lok Sabha to amend three laws governing Union Territory legislatures so that their elections can be held simultaneously. It has been referred to the same Joint Parliamentary Committee as the Constitution amendment Bill.

items.body: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
items.headline: Public Liability Insurance (Amendment) Rules, 2024 raise insurer liability and relief amounts
items.text: The Environment Ministry notified the Public Liability Insurance (Amendment) Rules, 2024, increasing the liability limits of insurers and specifying the relief amounts payable to victims of accidents involving hazardous substances.

items.headline: RTE Rules amended to permit holding back students in central government schools
items.text: The Ministry of Education notified the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (Amendment) Rules, 2024, which allow students in schools run by the central government to be held back in certain classes, altering the earlier no-detention approach.

items.body: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
items.headline: Draft Solid Waste Management Rules, 2024 released for public comment
items.text: The Environment Ministry released the draft Solid Waste Management Rules, 2024 and invited comments until February 7, 2025.

items.headline: Coal Ministry releases draft Coal Bearing Areas (Acquisition and Development) Amendment Bill, 2024
items.text: The Ministry of Coal released draft amendments to the Coal Bearing Areas (Acquisition and Development) Act. The draft provides lifetime leases for operational coal mines, integrates rehabilitation norms drawn from the 2013 land acquisition law, and creates a mechanism to denotify land for alternative uses.

items.headline: Winter Session of Parliament begins, scheduled to run till December 20, 2024
items.text: The Winter Session of Parliament commenced on November 25, 2024 with 19 sittings planned up to December 20, 2024. Bills listed for consideration included the Banking Laws (Amendment), Boilers, Bharatiya Vayuyan Vidheyak and Waqf (Amendment) Bills; Bills listed for introduction included the Merchant Shipping, Coastal Shipping and Indian Ports Bills.

items.headline: Supreme Court lays down directions on demolition of properties of accused persons
items.text: In Writ Petition (Civil) No. 295 of 2022, the Supreme Court held that authorities must be satisfied that demolition is the only available option and must give the affected party at least 15 days' prior notice specifying the unauthorised construction and the grounds. The directions do not cover structures in public places or demolitions ordered by a court.
items.why: Sets procedural safeguards against so-called punitive 'bulldozer' demolitions.

items.headline: CERC releases draft regulations for trading carbon credit certificates on power exchanges
items.text: The Central Electricity Regulatory Commission released draft Regulations on the trading of carbon credit certificates, enabling such certificates to be traded on power exchanges. Comments were invited until December 15, 2024.

items.headline: Five-judge SC bench: government entities cannot unilaterally appoint arbitrators
items.text: In Civil Appeal Nos. 9486-9487 of 2019, a five-judge bench of the Supreme Court held that clauses allowing a government entity to unilaterally appoint arbitrators in public-private contracts violate the guarantee of equality and equal protection before law under Article 14 of the Constitution.

items.headline: Seven-judge bench lays down test for minority status (Aligarh Muslim University v. Naresh Agarwal)
items.text: A seven-judge bench in Aligarh Muslim University v. Naresh Agarwal (C.A. No. 2286/2006) laid down the criteria for deciding whether an educational institution is a minority institution under Article 30, and left the question of AMU's status to a regular bench.

items.headline: Nine-judge bench on 'material resources of the community' under Article 39(b)
items.text: In Property Owners Association v. State of Maharashtra (C.A. No. 1012/2002) a nine-judge bench held by majority that not every privately owned resource is a 'material resource of the community' under Article 39(b).

items.headline: Nine-judge bench on States' power over industrial alcohol (State of U.P. v. Lalta Prasad Vaish)
items.text: A nine-judge bench of the Supreme Court in State of U.P. v. M/s Lalta Prasad Vaish and Sons (C.A. No. 151/2007) ruled on the power of States to regulate industrial alcohol, holding by majority that States retain legislative competence over it.

items.headline: Section 6A of the Citizenship Act upheld (In re: Section 6A of the Citizenship Act, 1955)
items.text: A Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court decided the challenge to Section 6A of the Citizenship Act, 1955, the special citizenship provision for migrants to Assam (W.P.(C) No. 274/2009), and upheld its validity.

items.headline: Disability percentage alone cannot bar admission to courses (Omkar v. Union of India)
items.text: In Omkar v. Union of India (C.A. No. 10611/2024) the Supreme Court held that the mere quantification of a candidate's disability cannot by itself disqualify them from admission to an educational course; their actual ability to pursue it must be assessed.

items.headline: Caste-based discrimination in prisons struck down (Sukanya Shantha v. Union of India)
items.text: In Sukanya Shantha v. Union of India (W.P.(C) No. 1404/2023) the Supreme Court held caste-based segregation and allocation of work in prisons unconstitutional and directed States to revise their prison manuals.

items.headline: SEBI board approves new passive fund framework and wider sustainable finance instruments
items.text: At its board meeting, SEBI approved phased extension of optional same-day settlement to the top 500 listed companies, a new mutual fund product with a Rs 10 lakh minimum investment, a separate regulatory framework for passively managed mutual funds with relaxed sponsor criteria, and an expanded framework covering social, sustainability and sustainability-linked bonds.

items.headline: SC: viewing or storing child sexual abuse material is an offence under POCSO
items.text: In Just Rights for Children Alliance v. S Harish, the Supreme Court set aside a Madras High Court judgment and held that possession of child sexual abuse material is an offence under the POCSO Act, 2012 even without intent to share it.
items.why: Clarifies criminal liability for possessing CSAM.

items.headline: Bombay High Court strikes down fact check unit provision in IT Rules
items.text: In Kunal Kamra v. Union of India, the Bombay High Court struck down the 2023 amendment to the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 that set up a government fact check unit, holding it violated free speech.

items.body: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
items.headline: Draft rules require anti-tobacco warnings on OTT platforms
items.text: The Health Ministry issued draft amendments to the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Rules, 2004 requiring non-skippable anti-tobacco messages in OTT content published after September 1, 2023. Comments were due by October 13, 2024.

items.headline: Uniform Code for marketing practices in medical devices released
items.text: The Department of Pharmaceuticals released a uniform code governing the promotion of medical devices. Claims must rest on up-to-date evidence, devices cannot be described as safe or free of side-effects without qualification, brand reminders are capped at Rs 1,000 in value, and ethics committees of industry associations must decide complaints within 90 days.

items.headline: 23rd Law Commission of India constituted for 2024-2027
items.text: The Ministry of Law and Justice constituted the 23rd Law Commission of India for the period September 1, 2024 to August 31, 2027. The Chairperson and Members were yet to be appointed.

items.headline: Draft Rules on interception, suspension and cybersecurity under Telecommunications Act, 2023
items.text: The DoT invited comments until September 27, 2024 on draft Rules under the Telecommunications Act, 2023 covering interception of communications, temporary suspension of services, telecom cybersecurity and designation of critical telecom infrastructure.

items.body: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
items.headline: Draft Remediation of Contaminated Sites Rules, 2024 released
items.text: The Environment Ministry released the draft Remediation of Contaminated Sites Rules, 2024 under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, laying down procedures for remediating sites contaminated by hazardous substances. Comments were due by October 20, 2024.

items.headline: Supreme Court constitutes National Task Force on safety of medical professionals
items.text: The Supreme Court set up a National Task Force to recommend measures to ensure the safety of medical professionals and safe working conditions, with an interim report due on September 10 and a final report by October 20, 2024.

items.headline: FEMA Non-debt Instruments Rules amended to allow equity swaps
items.text: The Foreign Exchange Management (Non-debt Instruments) Rules, 2019 were amended to allow equity swaps and to permit 100% foreign investment in white label ATM operations.

items.headline: Offshore Areas Mineral Trust and Auction Rules, 2024 notified
items.text: The Mines Ministry notified the Offshore Areas Mineral Trust Rules, 2024 (August 9) and the Offshore Areas Mineral (Auction) Rules, 2024 (August 14) under the Offshore Areas Mineral (Development and Regulation) Act, 2002.

items.headline: First Budget Session of 18th Lok Sabha concludes with 11 Bills introduced
items.text: The Budget Session, which began on July 22, 2024, concluded after 15 sittings. Eleven Bills were introduced, including the Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024, the Bharatiya Vayuyan Vidheyak, 2024, the Disaster Management (Amendment) Bill, 2024 and the Banking Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024.

items.headline: Lok Sabha passes Bharatiya Vayuyan Vidheyak, 2024 to replace Aircraft Act, 1934
items.text: The Lok Sabha passed the Bharatiya Vayuyan Vidheyak, 2024, which replaces the Aircraft Act, 1934. It adds regulation of aircraft design, retains DGCA, BCAS and AAIB, and provides a two-tier appeal mechanism.

items.body: Lok Sabha / Ministry of Minority Affairs
items.headline: Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024 introduced during Budget Session; JPC seeks comments
items.text: The Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024, introduced in the Lok Sabha during the Budget Session, limits waqf creation to persons practising Islam for at least five years, removes waqf by user and revises board composition. The Mussalman Wakf (Repeal) Bill, 2024 was also introduced; the JPC invited comments by September 11.
items.why: Among the most debated Bills of the year.

items.body: Lok Sabha / Ministry of Home Affairs
items.headline: Disaster Management (Amendment) Bill, 2024 introduced in Lok Sabha
items.text: The Disaster Management (Amendment) Bill, 2024, introduced during the Budget Session, empowers States to constitute Urban Disaster Management Authorities and State Disaster Response Forces.

items.headline: Banking Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024 introduced in Lok Sabha
items.text: The Banking Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024, introduced during the Budget Session, amends five banking-related Acts, including provisions on the definition of cash reserves and the tenure of directors of cooperative banks.

items.body: Parliament / Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
items.headline: Bills to replace colonial-era shipping laws introduced in Lok Sabha
items.text: The Carriage of Goods by Sea Bill, 2024 and the Bills of Lading Bill, 2024 were introduced in the Lok Sabha during the Budget Session to replace the Indian Carriage of Goods by Sea Act, 1925 and the Indian Bills of Lading Act, 1856. The Boilers Bill, 2024 was introduced in the Rajya Sabha to replace the Boilers Act, 1923.

items.body: Rajya Sabha / Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
items.headline: Oilfields (Regulation and Development) Amendment Bill, 2024 introduced in Rajya Sabha
items.text: The Oilfields (Regulation and Development) Amendment Bill, 2024 expands the definition of mineral oils, introduces a petroleum lease, and decriminalises offences by replacing them with fines.

items.headline: RBI issues Directions on treatment of wilful and large defaulters
items.text: The RBI (Treatment of Wilful Defaulters and Large Defaulters) Directions, 2024 cover borrowers or guarantors with wilful default of Rs 25 lakh or more, and set an identification committee, show-cause and review committee process with a personal hearing.

items.headline: Supreme Court (8:1) upholds States' power to tax mineral-bearing land
items.text: In Mineral Area Development Authority v. Steel Authority of India, a nine-judge bench held 8:1 that royalty is not a tax and that State legislatures can tax mineral-bearing land under Entry 50 of the State List. The MMDR Act, 1957 does not limit this power.
items.why: A major ruling on Centre-State taxation powers.

items.headline: Union Budget 2024-25 presented in Parliament
items.text: The Union Budget 2024-25 was presented on July 23, 2024, estimating total expenditure of Rs 48,20,512 crore and targeting a fiscal deficit of 4.9% of GDP.

items.headline: Budget Session 2024 begins; Economic Survey 2023-24 tabled
items.text: The Budget Session of Parliament began on July 22, 2024 and was scheduled to run till August 12 with 16 sittings; five Bills apart from Finance and Appropriation Bills were listed. The Economic Survey 2023-24 was tabled the same day.

items.headline: Draft Telecommunications (Adjudication and Appeal) Rules, 2024 released
items.text: The draft rules implement the adjudication framework of the Telecommunications Act, 2023: officers of joint secretary rank would conclude inquiries within 90 days (max 120), with appeals within 30 days to a Designated Appeals Committee.

items.body: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
items.headline: Draft amendments to Environment (Protection) Rules to give effect to Jan Vishwas Act
items.text: Comments were invited on draft amendments to the Environment (Protection) Rules, 1986 to give effect to the decriminalisation provisions of the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2023.

items.headline: RBI releases revised Master Directions on fraud risk management
items.text: The RBI issued three revised Master Directions on Fraud Risk Management applicable to banks and NBFCs.

items.headline: TRAI amends regulatory framework for broadcasting and cable services
items.text: TRAI amended its tariff, interconnection and quality of service regulations for broadcasting and cable services.

items.headline: Draft Digital Bharat Nidhi Rules under Telecommunications Act, 2023 released
items.text: The draft Telecommunications (Digital Bharat Nidhi) Rules, 2024 would operationalise the fund replacing the Universal Service Obligation Fund, financing telecom access in underserved areas and R&D. Comments were due by August 3, 2024.

items.headline: President Droupadi Murmu addresses joint sitting of Parliament
items.text: President Droupadi Murmu addressed a joint sitting of both Houses at the start of the 18th Lok Sabha, outlining the government's policy agenda across infrastructure, defence, the economy and development.

items.headline: SEBI board bars unregistered persons from inducing investments, mandates cybersecurity framework
items.text: At its board meeting SEBI decided to restrict unregistered persons from inducing securities investments, exempt certain university funds from FPI disclosure norms, and require regulated entities to adopt a cybersecurity framework by April 1, 2025.

items.headline: First session of 18th Lok Sabha opens; Om Birla elected Speaker
items.text: The first session of the 18th Lok Sabha ran from June 24 to July 3, 2024, alongside the 264th session of the Rajya Sabha. Om Birla was elected Speaker on June 26, 2024.

items.headline: High-level committee set up on examination reform and restructuring of NTA
items.text: A high-level committee chaired by Dr. K. Radhakrishnan was constituted to recommend reforms in the examination process, data security and the structure of the National Testing Agency, with its report due in August 2024.

items.headline: Draft guidelines to curb unsolicited commercial calls and messages released
items.text: The Department of Consumer Affairs released draft guidelines to prevent unsolicited business communication through calls, SMS and social media, based on consent and DND registry compliance. Comments were invited until July 21, 2024.

items.headline: CERC notifies new regulations for inter-state transmission licences
items.text: The CERC (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for grant of Transmission Licence) Regulations, 2024 replaced the 2009 regulations, exempting distribution licensees and bulk consumers from licensing for lines connecting to the inter-state system.

items.headline: Cinematograph (Adjudication of Penalty) Rules, 2024 notified
items.text: The Cinematograph (Adjudication of Penalty) Rules, 2024 were notified under the Cinematograph Act, 1952. They set the procedure for authorised officers to levy penalties for exhibition violations, with appellate oversight and powers of entry and evidence collection.

items.headline: Offshore Areas (Existence of Mineral Resources) Rules, 2024 notified
items.text: The Offshore Areas (Existence of Mineral Resources) Rules, 2024 set criteria for identifying offshore mineral-bearing areas for grant of production leases and composite licences, based on exploration and geological reports.

items.headline: New Union government formed after 2024 Lok Sabha general elections
items.text: Results of the general elections to the 18th Lok Sabha were declared, with members from 41 parties elected. The National Democratic Alliance formed the government, with the BJP winning 240 seats.

items.headline: Draft Central Excise Bill, 2024 released to replace Central Excise Act, 1944
items.text: The Finance Ministry released the draft Central Excise Bill, 2024 for comments. It would replace the Central Excise Act, 1944 on the levy and collection of excise duty on goods made in India, with self-assessment and appeals to the High Court.

items.headline: RBI notifies framework for self-regulatory organisations in FinTech
items.text: The RBI notified the Framework for Self-Regulatory Organisation(s) in the FinTech Sector, laying down eligibility criteria and operational standards for SROs, with the RBI remaining the apex regulator.

items.headline: IRDAI master circular on health insurance supersedes 55 earlier circulars
items.text: IRDAI issued the Master Circular on Health Insurance Business, superseding 55 earlier circulars. It requires insurers to offer products for all categories of individuals and to provide customer information sheets.

items.headline: Dam Safety Authority notifies regulations on surveillance and inspection of specified dams
items.text: The National Dam Safety Authority notified the Surveillance, Inspection and Hydrometeorological Station of Specified Dams Regulation, 2024, mandating dam monitoring, pre- and post-monsoon inspections and hydrometeorological stations.

items.headline: SEBI restricts sharing of real-time price data by market infrastructure institutions
items.text: SEBI issued norms under which market infrastructure institutions may share real-time price data with third parties only where needed for orderly market functioning or regulatory compliance.

items.headline: SEBI consults on mutual fund investments in overseas funds with Indian exposure
items.text: SEBI issued a consultation paper proposing that Indian mutual funds be allowed to invest in overseas funds that have exposure to Indian securities, capped at 20% of their assets.

items.headline: RBI draft prudential framework for project finance
items.text: The RBI released draft directions on a prudential framework for project finance, covering exposure limits, stress resolution and provisioning for infrastructure and commercial real estate projects.

items.headline: SEBI board approves higher NRI/OCI participation in IFSC FPIs and anti-market abuse norms for AMCs
items.text: At its board meeting SEBI approved allowing NRIs and OCIs up to 100% participation in FPIs based in IFSCs, and approved a mechanism for asset management companies to deter market abuse, among other decisions.

items.headline: RBI issues draft directions for electronic trading platforms
items.text: Draft RBI directions propose authorisation requirements for electronic trading platforms dealing in eligible securities and derivatives, including three years of infrastructure experience and minimum net worth of Rs 5 crore.

items.headline: Draft Explosives Bill, 2024 released to replace Explosives Act, 1884
items.text: The draft Explosives Bill, 2024 was put out for public feedback to replace the Explosives Act, 1884. It revises penalties, including raising fines for illegal manufacture, import or export from Rs 5,000 to Rs 1 lakh, and updates licensing.

items.headline: Supreme Court rejects pleas for return to paper ballots or 100% VVPAT verification
items.text: The Supreme Court dismissed petitions seeking a return to paper ballots or full VVPAT slip verification. It directed that symbol loading units be sealed and stored with EVMs for at least 45 days after results, and allowed checks for tampering on 5% of EVMs on request.
items.why: Sets safeguards on EVM use in elections.

items.headline: RBI circular lays down route for small finance banks to become universal banks
items.text: An RBI circular permits voluntary conversion of small finance banks into universal banks subject to conditions such as five years of satisfactory performance, listed shares, a minimum net worth of Rs 1,000 crore and recent profitability.

items.headline: RBI draft guidelines on transparency in digital loan aggregation
items.text: The RBI released draft guidelines requiring lending service providers that aggregate loan offers to display unbiased offers from multiple lenders and avoid dark patterns that could mislead borrowers.

items.headline: RBI issues Asset Reconstruction Companies Directions, 2024
items.text: The RBI issued the RBI (Asset Reconstruction Companies) Directions, 2024, setting registration requirements including minimum net owned funds of Rs 300 crore and governance standards for entities that acquire stressed assets from lenders.

items.headline: TRAI recommends wider sharing of telecom infrastructure and spectrum
items.text: TRAI recommended permitting sharing of passive and active infrastructure among telecom licensees, with restrictions on core network elements, and mandatory sharing of government-funded infrastructure.

items.headline: Law Ministry sets up committee on welfare measures for queer persons
items.text: The Ministry of Law and Justice constituted a committee chaired by the Cabinet Secretary to recommend welfare measures for queer persons. This follows the Supreme Court's October 2023 judgment in the challenge relating to the Special Marriage Act, 1954.
items.why: Implements a Supreme Court direction from the same-sex marriage case.

items.headline: RBI draft directions bring offline payment aggregators under regulation
items.text: The RBI invited comments on draft directions extending regulation to offline payment aggregators, requiring authorisation by March 31, 2025, with minimum net worth of Rs 15 crore initially rising to Rs 25 crore by 2028.

items.headline: TRAI recommends regulatory sandbox framework for telecom
items.text: TRAI recommended a regulatory sandbox allowing innovative telecom services to be tested for up to 12 months, with oversight arrangements and funding proposed through the Digital Bharat Nidhi.

items.headline: SC stays Centre's notification of PIB Fact Check Unit under IT Rules
items.text: The Supreme Court stayed the Centre's 20 March 2024 notification setting up the Fact Check Unit under the amended IT Rules, 2023 until the Bombay High Court finally decides the challenge by Kunal Kamra, the Editors Guild and others. It said the challenge raised serious questions about free speech under Article 19(1)(a).

items.headline: SC orders SBI to disclose all electoral bond details, including unique bond numbers
items.text: In the electoral bonds case (Association for Democratic Reforms v. Union of India), the Constitution Bench directed the State Bank of India to disclose all details of electoral bonds in its possession, including the alphanumeric bond numbers that match donors to recipient parties, and to file an affidavit of compliance. SBI filed its compliance affidavit on 21 March.

items.headline: Cinematograph (Certification) Rules, 2024 notified with new age-based UA categories
items.text: The I&B Ministry notified the Cinematograph (Certification) Rules, 2024, replacing the 1983 Rules. They introduce age-based markers UA 7+, UA 13+ and UA 16+, require at least one-third women on certification boards, and were accompanied by accessibility guidelines for audio description and captions.

items.body: High Level Committee on Simultaneous Elections
items.headline: Kovind-led High Level Committee recommends 'One Nation, One Election'
items.text: The High Level Committee chaired by former President Ram Nath Kovind submitted its report to the President recommending constitutional amendments to hold simultaneous elections to the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies, followed by local body elections.

items.headline: Uttarakhand Uniform Civil Code Bill receives President's assent
items.text: The Uniform Civil Code, Uttarakhand Bill, 2024, passed by the State Assembly in February, received the President's assent. This made Uttarakhand the first State after independence to enact a uniform civil code covering marriage, divorce, succession and live-in relationships.

items.headline: SCBA President's letter seeking to stall electoral bonds verdict draws disowning by Executive Committee
items.text: SCBA President Adish C. Aggarwala wrote to the President of India asking her to seek a Presidential Reference and withhold enforcement of the electoral bonds judgment. On 13 March the SCBA Executive Committee condemned and disowned the letter, and on 18 March the Supreme Court dismissed his later letter to the CJI as 'publicity oriented'.

items.headline: Committee on Digital Competition Law proposes ex-ante Digital Competition Act
items.text: The Committee on Digital Competition Law recommended a Digital Competition Act to regulate 'Systemically Significant Digital Enterprises' in advance (ex-ante), along with a draft Bill; public comments were invited till 15 April 2024.

items.headline: Centre notifies Citizenship (Amendment) Rules, 2024, operationalising the CAA
items.text: The Ministry of Home Affairs notified the Citizenship (Amendment) Rules, 2024, setting out the process and documents for eligible applicants from Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Pakistan to seek citizenship under the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019. Several petitions challenging the Rules followed in the Supreme Court, which issued notice on 19 March.

items.headline: Law Commission (Report No. 289) recommends separate law to protect trade secrets
items.text: In its 289th Report 'Trade Secrets and Economic Espionage', forwarded on 5 March 2024, the Law Commission recommended a standalone law to protect trade secrets based on unfair competition principles, with exceptions for whistleblowers and the public interest, and separate treatment of economic espionage.

items.headline: Seven-judge bench in Sita Soren v. Union of India: no immunity for legislators taking bribes
items.text: A seven-judge Constitution Bench unanimously overruled the 1998 P.V. Narasimha Rao judgment, holding that Articles 105 and 194 do not protect MPs or MLAs from prosecution for taking bribes to vote or speak in the legislature, and that the offence is complete when the bribe is accepted.
items.why: Removed a 26-year-old shield against prosecution of legislators for bribery.

items.headline: Eminent jurist and Senior Advocate Fali S. Nariman passes away
items.text: Fali S. Nariman, one of India's foremost constitutional lawyers and a former Additional Solicitor General, passed away on 21 February 2024. He appeared in many landmark cases, including the Second Judges case that led to the collegium system.

items.headline: SC in Kuldeep Kumar v. UT of Chandigarh declares AAP-Congress candidate Chandigarh Mayor
items.text: Using its Article 142 powers in Kuldeep Kumar v. Union Territory of Chandigarh (SLP(C) No. 2998/2024), the Supreme Court held that the presiding officer had deliberately invalidated eight ballots and declared Kuldeep Kumar the elected Mayor. It also started proceedings under Section 340 CrPC against presiding officer Anil Masih for making a false statement before the Court.

items.headline: Constitution Bench in ADR v. Union of India strikes down Electoral Bond Scheme
items.text: In Association for Democratic Reforms v. Union of India (W.P.(C) No. 880 of 2017), a five-judge bench unanimously struck down the Electoral Bond Scheme and related amendments, holding they violated voters' right to information under Article 19(1)(a) and that unlimited corporate funding was manifestly arbitrary. SBI was directed to give bond details to the ECI by 6 March for publication by 13 March.
items.why: A landmark ruling on transparency in political funding, weeks before the general elections.

items.headline: Law Commission (Report No. 287) recommends compulsory registration of NRI/OCI marriages
items.text: In its 287th Report forwarded on 15 February 2024, the Law Commission recommended a comprehensive central law requiring compulsory registration of marriages between NRIs/OCIs and Indian citizens, and covering divorce, maintenance, child custody and service of summons. It also proposed amending the Passports Act to require marital status declarations.

items.headline: 17th Lok Sabha's final session ends; 221 Bills passed over its term
items.text: The last session of the 17th Lok Sabha ran from January 31 to February 10, 2024, extended by a day. Over its term Parliament passed 221 Bills, including the Women's Reservation Bill, the Digital Personal Data Protection Bill and the three Bills replacing the IPC, CrPC and Evidence Act.

items.headline: Parliament passes Jammu and Kashmir Local Bodies Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024
items.text: Parliament passed the Jammu and Kashmir Local Bodies Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024 during the session that ended on February 10. It amends three local body laws of the UT to extend reservation to OBCs in panchayats and municipalities and makes the State Election Commission responsible for these elections.

items.headline: Parliament amends Scheduled Castes and Tribes lists for Odisha and Andhra Pradesh
items.text: Parliament passed two Bills amending the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950 and the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950 in the session ending February 10, 2024. Communities such as Muka Dora (Odisha) and Bondo Porja and Konda Savaras (Andhra Pradesh) were added to the ST lists.

items.headline: Parliament passes Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Bill, 2024 against paper leaks
items.text: Parliament passed the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Bill, 2024, introduced on 5 February. It penalises paper leaks, tampering and impersonation in central recruitment and entrance exams with 3 to 5 years' imprisonment and fines up to Rs 10 lakh, and 5 to 10 years with a minimum Rs 1 crore fine for organised paper-leak rackets. All offences are cognisable and non-bailable.

items.headline: Parliament passes Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Amendment Bill decriminalising offences
items.text: Lok Sabha passed the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Amendment Bill, 2024 on 8 February 2024, two days after Rajya Sabha. It replaces imprisonment for several violations with penalties of Rs 10,000 to Rs 15 lakh decided by adjudicating officers, with appeals to the NGT. It applies at first to Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan and the Union Territories.

items.body: Parliamentary Standing Committee on Law and Justice
items.headline: Parliamentary panel recommends separate regulator for legal education, curbing BCI's role
items.text: The Standing Committee on Personnel, Public Grievances, Law and Justice, chaired by Sushil Kumar Modi, submitted its report on strengthening legal education on 7 February 2024. It recommended a National Council for Legal Education and Research to take over regulation of legal education beyond Bar eligibility, a uniform curriculum, curbs on substandard law colleges and paid internships.

items.headline: Law Commission (Report No. 285) recommends retaining criminal defamation
items.text: The 22nd Law Commission, in its 285th Report 'The Law on Criminal Defamation' forwarded on 31 January 2024, recommended that criminal defamation be kept in the scheme of criminal laws, reasoning that the right to reputation flows from Article 21 and needs adequate protection.

items.headline: Law Commission (Report No. 284) proposes tougher law on damage to public property during protests
items.text: In its 284th Report forwarded on 31 January 2024, the Law Commission recommended amending the Prevention of Damage to Public Property Act, 1984, including a rebuttable presumption of guilt, holding leaders who call such actions liable for abetment, and requiring the accused to deposit the value of the damage as a condition for bail.

items.headline: FEMA non-debt instruments rules amended to allow direct listing of Indian companies abroad
items.text: The Foreign Exchange Management (Non-debt Instruments) Amendment Rules, 2024, notified on 24 January 2024, permit Indian public companies to directly list their shares on permitted international exchanges.

items.headline: Mineral auction rules amended to auction exploration licences
items.text: The Ministry of Mines notified the Mineral (Auction) Amendment Rules, 2024 under the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957. They lay down procedures for auctioning exploration licences, including for minerals such as lithium, cobalt, silver and gold.
items.why: Operationalises the 2023 amendment to the MMDR Act.

items.body: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
items.headline: Draft End-of-Life Vehicles (Management) Rules, 2024 released
items.text: The Environment Ministry released the draft End-of-Life Vehicles (Management) Rules, 2024 under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. They set recycling targets and assign responsibilities to vehicle producers and owners.
items.why: Brings extended producer responsibility to vehicles.

items.headline: Centre issues Guidelines for Regulation of Coaching Centres, 2024
items.text: The Ministry of Education released guidelines for regulating coaching centres, setting out registration requirements and operating standards for them, to be implemented by States.

items.headline: Draft Indian Stamp Bill, 2023 released to replace the 1899 Stamp Act
items.text: The Finance Ministry released the draft Indian Stamp Bill, 2023 for public consultation on 17 January 2024, proposing to replace the Indian Stamp Act, 1899; comments were invited till 15 February 2024.

items.headline: Electricity Rules amended to mandate cost-reflective tariffs, cap open access surcharge
items.text: The Ministry of Power notified the Electricity (Amendment) Rules, 2024 on January 10 and the Electricity (Second Amendment) Rules, 2024 on January 17. They require cost-reflective tariffs and cap surcharges on open access consumers under the Electricity Act, 2003.

items.headline: SC in Bilkis Yakub Rasool v. Union of India quashes remission granted to 11 convicts
items.text: The Supreme Court set aside the Gujarat government's orders granting premature release to the 11 convicts in the Bilkis Bano gang-rape and murder case, holding that Gujarat was not the appropriate government because the trial took place in Maharashtra, and ordered them back to jail. On 19 January it rejected their pleas for more time and ordered them to surrender by 21 January.

items.headline: SC accepts Second National Judicial Pay Commission recommendations; orders States to clear arrears by Feb 29
items.text: In All India Judges Association v. Union of India, the Supreme Court accepted the recommendations of the Second National Judicial Pay Commission on pay, pension and allowances of judicial officers, directed States to pay the arrears by 29 February 2024, and asked High Courts to set up committees to oversee implementation.
